# Tool server (MCP) tools

What an assistant connected to the tool server can call: 168 tools. The default list is the core pack, at most 10 tools; every other family is opt-in. The script API is the product: an assistant works by writing a script ([the kit](script-kit/ctx.md)), not by calling many tools. `?` marks an optional input.

## MutinyBIM core

Family `core`: Write, check, preview and land scripts that read and change the model, save a part script's parts, and four reads to look before writing.

Turn it on: `/mcp` (the default list).

### bim_script_reference

Start here before writing a MutinyBIM script; read the index once per thread. No arguments: whether scripts can run here, the example scripts, the workflow, the kit's functions by name. search: a topic ("rooftop unit", "drain slope", "sheet per level"). topic: one function or recipe by name, whole. example: one whole example script ("rooftop-unit", "small-office", "plumbing-riser", "electrical-room"). command: one ctx.edit command's fields. library: list or read saved scripts.

Input: `example`?, `search`?, `topic`?, `command`?, `library`?, `key`?, `version`?

### bim_check_output

Lint and syntax of a script with line numbers, kit calls and commands that don't exist, and what its reads send (with model_id); or the kernel's checks on an output. Runs and saves nothing. The answer's script_id names the script in later calls.

Input: `project_id`?, `model_id`?, `level`?, `zone`?, `script`?, `selection`?, `output`?

### bim_run_script

Preview: run a script on this thread's sealed machine (no network, 1 GB, 30 s, 2 MB) and check its output. Saves nothing; returns what would change, apply_with and script_id (send the id, not the text, next time).

Input: `project_id`?, `model_id`?, `level`?, `zone`?, `script`, `values`?, `selection`?

### bim_apply_output

Land bim_run_script's apply_with.args (unchanged) as one undo step after the person approves; re-runs and lands only what was previewed. Outside clients send output + provenance instead of script.

Input: `project_id`?, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`, `script`?, `output`?, `provenance`?, `values`?, `selection`?, `output_hash`, `label`, `steps`, `changes`, `approval`

### bim_save_part_type

Save bim_run_script's part types (apply_with.args) and the script version to the firm library after the person approves; re-runs and saves only what was previewed.

Input: `project_id`?, `model_id`?, `script`, `values`?, `output_hash`, `parts`, `save_as`?

### bim_model_summary

Counts by element kind, the areas (level / zone / discipline) the model has, systems with their total airflow, open validation issues, the Not placed yet list (parts that exist before they are drawn, each with its circuit), open questions and assumptions, and the revision this was read at. Start here, then read one area at a time.

Input: `project_id`?, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `questions`?

### bim_query_elements

List elements by kind, class, area and discipline with the facts needed to plan an edit (sizes in inches, lengths and positions in feet, airflow in CFM). Returns the revision read and the total matched. Filter by level/zone on large models.

Input: `project_id`?, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `kinds`?, `class`?, `discipline`?, `ids`?, `limit`?, `why`?, `if_removed`?

### bim_inspect_network

For one element: what it connects to, and the path from it up to its equipment with airflow on each piece. Use before editing a branch, run or terminal.

Input: `project_id`?, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `element_id`

### bim_validation_issues

Open validation issues (disconnected connectors, undersized branches, …) with the elements involved and the revision read.

Input: `project_id`?, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `limit`?

## Model reads and everyday edits

Family `model`: Schedule rows, levels, views and sheets, linked models, surfaces; previews and the everyday part edits; pictures, printing and issuing sheets; coordination lint.

Turn it on: `/packs/model/mcp`, `--packs model`, or `bim_enable_pack` in a session.

### bim_schedule_read

Rows of a schedule view (or an ad hoc v2 definition): columns with unit and whether a cell edits per instance or per type, rows as [row_key, ...cells] (limit ≤200 from offset), totals, and explain text for locked cells. Panel/feeder form schedules return what prints. No schedule: lists schedule views. Read-only.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `schedule`?, `definition`?, `offset`?, `limit`?, `columns`?, `explain`?

### bim_list_part_types

Part types you can place, in every discipline: the model's own types first, then the starter library's. Each lists its type values, the instance parameters you can set (with units and choices) and its connectors. Also returns the model's levels. Read this before bim_place_part.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `category`?, `search`?, `limit`?

### bim_list_levels

The model's levels (name, elevation in feet, and the linked storey a level was made from), and for each linked model its storeys placed where the model shows them, with what bim_sync_linked_levels would do to each. Read this before adding, moving or syncing levels.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`

### bim_list_views_and_sheets

Every view (plan, ceiling plan, section, 3D, detail view) with its level, scale and the sheet it is on, and every sheet with its viewports, notes and live blocks (text now, unresolved fields). Use before creating or placing so you reuse names and ids.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`

### bim_list_linked_models

The models linked under this project's Building Model (the architect's model, structure, existing MEP, our own Revit model): where each came from, the version shown and every version with its status (queued, converting, ready, failed), whether it is lined up (and what fixes it when not), its position adjustment in feet, the latest export from Revit and Docs files still coming in. Read this before levels from the architect, line-up or anything that depends on a linked model.

Input: `project_id`

### bim_surfaces_at

Floor (or roof) under a placed part or a point, and the ceiling, roof and structure over it, each with its height and source (stated host, space ceiling height, our slabs, linked slabs/roofs/ceilings). Give element_id, or x_ft, y_ft and level.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `element_id`?, `x_ft`?, `y_ft`?, `level`?

### bim_describe_commands

The exact fields of a command family a MutinyBIM tool advertises in short form (bim_draw_detail items, bim_modify_detail operation, bim_set_system_design pipe_design and fittings, bim_route_run system_kind and from / to, bim_save_electrical_type entry, bim_preview_one_line / bim_layout_one_line diagram and hints). With only tool: its families; with field: its variants or schema; with variant: that one's schema. Reads no model; free.

Input: `tool`, `field`?, `variant`?

### bim_preview_part_edit

Dry run: what one of the part edit tools would change at the revision you read (elements changed, removed, connections cut), or the reason it would be refused. Saves nothing and needs no approval.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `tool`, `args`

### bim_preview_route_edit

Dry run of bim_route_run, bim_connect_runs, bim_disconnect_run, bim_route_flex, bim_resize_run, bim_slide_branch, bim_swap_fitting, bim_offset_run, bim_change_elevation, bim_set_fitting_coefficient_override, bim_set_system_design, bim_set_slope, bim_place_pipe_accessory, bim_split_run, bim_resize_stretch, bim_drag_run or bim_set_duct_insulation at the revision you read: the elements it would create or change, or the plain reason it would be refused. Saves nothing and needs no approval.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `tool`, `args`

### bim_preview_views_sheets_edit

Preview one views/sheets command, or batch_documents { label, commands: [...] } (≤500, all or nothing, one approval), at the latest revision, unsaved: what would change or why it'd be refused, plus a preview_token. Save with bim_apply_views_sheets_edit: same command, base_revision = the returned revision, the token. Commands: create_view (schedules: props.schedule), create_3d_view, set_3d_view_camera, set_3d_crop_box, rename_view, duplicate_view, delete_view, set_view_properties (plans: props.circuitGraphics), set_view_crop, create_sheet, set_sheet_properties (incl. revisions), delete_sheet, place_viewport, move_viewport, resize_viewport, set_viewport_scale, set_viewport_north_arrow, remove_viewport, add/update/delete_drawing_item (shape callout: 3 points, callout.viewId), create/edit/resize/move/delete_text_note; live blocks: add_field_block { itemId, sheetId, at or at_in, block? } (no block: the load summary; block.table { kind: ventilation|pressurization|gas, scope? }: that table), edit_field_block; spaces: create_space, edit_space (estimateCounting max|actual_only|allocation_only|null), delete_spaces, make_spaces_from_rooms, place_space_in_walls { spaceId, levelId, seed } (a room from the walls around a point), split_space { spaceId, line, typedLoadsTo } (sub-rooms under the room; typedLoadsTo names the sub-room, e.g. 101A, that keeps loads not by area: required when it has any), merge_space_children { spaceId }, create/edit/delete_zone(s) (servedBy), place/calibrate/edit/delete_underlay(s); loads (any trade): create_load (anchor space/zone = estimate), move_load, split_load, edit_load_point (servedBy), set_load_allocation_policy; questions (no one has to answer; nothing is due): add_question { questions: [{ questionId, text, askOf, anchor: { elementIds }, type? assumption, blocksIssue?, askedBefore? }] }, answer_question { questionId, answer, status? assumed, outcome? judgment_recorded|design_revision, links? [{ kind: branch|determination, ref }] }, reply_question { questionId, text }, decline_question { questionId, note?, not_in_scope?, keep_closed? reason }, take_over_question { questionId }, forward_question { questionId, askOf }, set_question_status { questionIds, status withdrawn|open (declined: owner only) }, edit_question, delete_questions; stacks: name_stacks { stacks: [{ stackId, pipeId, number? }] }, edit_stack, delete_stacks, set_stack_checks { baseClearanceDiameters }. Kernel fields: mm (sheet positions, note sizes: paper). Standalone tools' names convert: crop_min_ft/crop_max_ft, far_clip_ft, cut_height_ft, top_ft, bottom_ft, view_depth_ft, center_in, size_in, level/scale atop create_view / set_view_properties. Unknown keys are refused by name.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `command`

### bim_apply_views_sheets_edit

Save exactly the change bim_preview_views_sheets_edit returned: the same command (one views/sheets command or a batch_documents of up to 500), its base_revision and its preview_token. Anything different is refused before it is sent, so what the person approves is what saves. Retrying the same call never saves it twice. If someone changed the same things since the preview, nothing is saved and you get a conflict: preview again.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`, `preview_token`, `command`

### bim_render_view_image

Draw one view (floor or ceiling plan, section, 3D view, detail or drafting view, schedule) from the last saved revision as a PNG you can look at, exactly as it prints: linework, tags, dimensions, notes, crop. Use it after edits to check the drawing reads right (overlaps, clipped notes, missing tags). Optional: a region (view feet in the view's own frame, or paper inches from the drawing's top-left), elements to frame and outline in red, resolution. Returns the image, the revision drawn and the paper size.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `view`, `region_ft`?, `region_in`?, `focus_ids`?, `dpi`?, `max_px`?, `highlight_ids`?, `keep_copy`?

### bim_render_sheet_image

Draw one sheet from the last saved revision as a PNG you can look at, exactly as it prints: border, viewports at scale with titles, notes, schedules, title block. Use it to check a sheet's layout before printing or issuing. Optional: a region in paper inches from the sheet's top-left (to read small text), elements or drawn items to outline in red, resolution. A whole 36 x 24 sheet at the default size is an overview; zoom with region_in to read notes.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `sheet`, `region_in`?, `dpi`?, `max_px`?, `highlight_ids`?, `keep_copy`?

### bim_print_sheet_pdf

Draw one sheet from the last saved revision of the model to a vector PDF at true scale and return a download link valid for 5 minutes, with the revision printed and the file's sha256. It prints what is saved; edits still in flight are not included. print_notes: viewports past the drawing area, labels the PDF font printed as plain text (1⅜ as 1-3/8). Does not issue the sheet.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `sheet`

### bim_print_view_pdf

Draw one view (plan, section, 3D, detail or drafting view, schedule) on its own from the last saved revision to a vector PDF sized to the view at its scale, and return a download link valid for 5 minutes with the revision and sha256. For a sheet use bim_print_sheet_pdf; for several sheets in one PDF, bim_print_set_pdf. Does not issue anything.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `view`

### bim_print_set_pdf

Draw sheets from the last saved revision to one vector PDF (a page per sheet, true scale, binding order G, A, M, P, E… then number, or the order given); returns each sheet's page, the revision, sha256 and a 5-minute link. Records the print for bim_issue_set; print_notes as bim_print_sheet_pdf. Does not issue.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `sheets`?, `title`?

### bim_issue_set

Issue sheets: one edit adds add_revision to each sheet, the model is captured, the set drawn only from the capture, stored write-once and filed in the project Workspace. Nothing is issued if anything saved since expected_revision, the revision exists, or a sheet draws differently than in the last bim_print_set_pdf (live schedules; print and check again, or accept_changes_since_print once checked). Retry-safe.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `name`, `expected_revision`, `sheets`?, `add_revision`?, `accept_changes_since_print`?

### bim_place_part

Place any part (equipment, air terminal, receptacle, panel, light, plumbing fixture…) on a level at a plan position in feet. No location: the part is planned (exists for circuits, schedules and the one-line, waits in Not placed yet). part_id draws a planned part, or with unplace takes one off the drawing. A starter-library or firm-library type (from_firm_library) is added to the model with the part. Values are checked against the type's parameters; a bad value is refused with the reason.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `type_id`?, `part_id`?, `unplace`?, `from_firm_library`?, `level_id`?, `x_ft`?, `y_ft`?, `level_hint`?, `space_hint`?, `note`?, `height_above_level_ft`?, `rotation_deg`?, `mark`?, `values`?, `mount`?, `on_plane_id`?, `intakes`?, `discipline`?, `equipment_list`?

### bim_move_elements

Move parts (and equipment with its connected ducts) by an offset in feet; parts can also move up or down. Tags follow.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `element_ids`, `dx_ft`, `dy_ft`, `dz_ft`?

### bim_rotate_elements

Rotate parts about their insertion point (one part) or a pivot / their centre (several).

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `element_ids`, `angle_deg`, `about_x_ft`?, `about_y_ft`?

### bim_copy_elements

Copy parts by an offset in feet. Copies keep the type and values but start without a mark.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `element_ids`, `dx_ft`, `dy_ft`

### bim_delete_elements

Delete parts, levels or other elements. If anything depends on them (tags, connections, parts on a level), the default refuses and lists them; choose disconnect or cascade to say what happens. The result says exactly what was removed.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `element_ids`, `if_dependents`?

### bim_set_parameters

Set a part's own values (scope instance) or its type's values, shared by every part of that type (scope type). Values are validated; type values can't be set at instance scope.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `element_id`, `scope`, `values`?, `mark`?, `mount`?, `intakes`?

### bim_move_wall

Move a wall by an offset in feet. The walls joined to it follow (their ends at its corners move with it, and walls teed into it stretch to stay on its face), so corners stay closed; its doors, windows, tags and room dimensions follow. disjoin: true leaves the joined walls where they are (Revit's Disjoin).

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `dx_ft`, `dy_ft`, `disjoin`?, `element_id`?, `wall_id`?

### bim_lint_configure

Once per session: how each saved edit's `lint` block checks (defaults: tolerance 0.5 in., clearances 1 in. services / 2 in. structure, radius 10 ft; snapshot after_edit adds a picture). Saved per thread (for=me: your model default). Returns settings and rules not available.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `ruleset`?, `tolerance_in`?, `soft_clearance_in`?, `structure_clearance_in`?, `scope_radius_ft`?, `include_linked`?, `max_findings`?, `snapshot`?, `disabled_rules`?, `for`?, `reset`?

### bim_lint_check

Every finding on the model, a level, or around ids, with the ruleset and tolerance used. Required (include_linked) before calling anything clash-free; ruleset issue before issuing. 25 a page.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `ids`?, `level`?, `ruleset`?, `include_linked`?, `include_accepted`?, `offset`?

### bim_status_snapshot

End of a batch: counts, findings by rule, this thread's last edits, up to 3 small pictures (last-edited plan, sheet, a 3D view, or those named). Say what you see.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `views`?, `sheets`?, `max_images`?

## Drafting and annotation

Family `drafting`: Dimensions, tags, notes with leaders, detail linework and detail components.

Turn it on: `/packs/drafting/mcp`, `--packs drafting`, or `bim_enable_pack` in a session.

### bim_list_view_annotations

Every dimension, tag, note, line, rectangle and cloud in a plan, section, detail view or on a sheet: id, what it prints (dimension values, tag words, note text), points (view feet, or paper inches on a sheet), its paper box, the elements a dimension or tag follows and any it lost (orphaned), note leaders, and which annotations overlap. Use it before editing a detail or tidying a plan.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `owner`

### bim_add_dimension

Dimension in a plan, section or detail view. kind: linear (horizontal / vertical), aligned, angular (vertex, two points), radial / diameter (centre, a point on it), arc_length (centre, start, end), spot_elevation / spot_coordinate (the point, then the text). Two points, or more with chain continuous or baseline. A point follows an element (element_id + anchor; updates when the model moves) or is fixed in view feet. offset_in: the line's distance from the first point on paper (sign picks the side). Text override, prefix, suffix, style optional.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `view`, `kind`, `points`, `direction`?, `chain`?, `offset_in`?, `text_override`?, `prefix`?, `suffix`?, `style`?

### bim_auto_dimension

Deterministic dimensions for elements in a plan or section: mode each puts one aligned dimension along every run, wall or grid given (its start to end, offset beside it); mode chain puts one continuous string across them (horizontal or vertical) through each one's centreline, ordered along the string. All of it is one edit and every dimension follows its element.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `view`, `element_ids`, `mode`, `direction`?, `offset_in`?

### bim_add_tag

Tag one element in a plan or section. template auto picks by kind (duct or pipe size, terminal mark + CFM, equipment or fixture mark), or name one; fields lists parameters, one per line. The words always come from the element. at_ft places the head; absent, the first clear spot beside it. Returns looks: what it overlaps or crosses.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `view`, `element_id`, `template`?, `fields`?, `leader`?, `at_ft`?, `text_height_in`?, `style`?

### bim_preview_auto_tag

Tag all in a plan or section, previewed: everything of the categories, each tag at the first spot beside its element clear of linework and other annotations; existing tags stay. Returns what each will say, what couldn't be tagged and why, and a preview_token for bim_auto_tag_view.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `view`, `categories`, `leaders`?, `include_tagged`?, `text_height_in`?, `style`?

### bim_auto_tag_view

Apply the tags bim_preview_auto_tag returned (same arguments, its base_revision and preview_token) as one edit. Refused if the model changed since the preview: preview again.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `view`, `categories`, `leaders`?, `include_tagged`?, `text_height_in`?, `style`?, `base_revision`, `preview_token`

### bim_add_note

A rich text note (bold, italic, underline, lists, sizes; prints as shown) in a plan, section, detail view or on a sheet, with leaders to points, each with an optional elbow and an arrow, dot, tick or none. Points are view feet, or paper inches on a sheet (at_in). The box stays paper-sized at any scale.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `owner`, `text`?, `paragraphs`?, `at`, `width_in`?, `text_height_in`?, `leaders`?

### bim_edit_annotation

Change one annotation by id (from bim_list_view_annotations): move it by dx / dy (view feet, or paper inches on a sheet) or auto_place a tag clear beside its element; change a dimension's text override / prefix / suffix / offset / style or points (as in bim_add_dimension); a tag's template, fields, leader, elbow or style; a note's leaders; spread tags (item_id + item_ids) clear of each other; or delete it. Tag edits return looks (what it overlaps or crosses). One per call; for many, bim_apply_views_sheets_edit with a batch.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `owner`, `item_id`, `action`, `dx`?, `dy`?, `auto_place`?, `points`?, `offset_in`?, `text_override`?, `prefix`?, `suffix`?, `style`?, `template`?, `fields`?, `leader`?, `tag_style`?, `elbow`?, `item_ids`?, `leaders`?

### bim_set_tag_text

Replace the text of a model-linked tag.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `text`, `element_id`?, `tag_id`?

### bim_list_tag_styles

The model's tag styles (lines with {field} placeholders, text height, leader, box, default_for kinds, tags using each) and the field names a style can use.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`

### bim_save_tag_style

A named tag look many tags share; changing it changes them all. style (id or name) changes or deletes one; without it, creates one named name, or from a preset (bim_list_tag_styles). lines: words and {field paths} per printed line, e.g. ["{size}[ {insulation}]"], ["{pipe.size}", "{pipe.length_lf}"]. box: true, false or a shape. orientation along: words follow the run. applies_to: kinds it labels; default_for: kinds whose new tags take it. "" clears prefix / suffix. delete: true removes an unused style.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `style`?, `name`?, `lines`?, `text_height_in`?, `leader`?, `box`?, `prefix`?, `suffix`?, `orientation`?, `units`?, `applies_to`?, `default_for`?, `preset`?, `delete`?

### bim_apply_tag_style

Put the tags in a plan or section (all, or only kinds / item_ids) on one tag style in one edit; their words, size, box and leader then follow it.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `view`, `style`, `kinds`?, `item_ids`?

### bim_list_detail_components

The 2D detail component library: id, name, category (duct, pipe, supports, valves, anchors, structure, insulation), default size in inches, and whether it stretches between two points (linear: flex duct, threaded rod). Use the id as `symbol` in bim_draw_detail.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`

### bim_draw_detail

Draw up to 500 items in a detail view, plan, section or sheet as one edit, on BIM conventions: detail lines are separate elements joined at their ends, so rect (four joined lines), polygon (inscribed or circumscribed), chain (lines through points, optionally closed; polyline is the same) make one line per side, ids <item id>-0, -1, …. Also line, arc (centre, start, end), arc_radius (start, end, radius, bulge side), arc_tangent (continues a line), circle, spline, region (hatch pattern, or masking; a closed sketch boundary), component (a library symbol at a point, rotated, mirrored, sized), repeat (a symbol repeated from one point to another), batt (insulation of a thickness between two points); on a sheet, figure (frame corner/opposite) with chart (plumbing.hunter_curve, live) or file_id + file_name (workspace PNG/JPEG). Each takes an optional line_style (the usual way to pick linework); weight (default medium) and pattern (default solid) override it; category is the view show / hide group; group makes a detail group (select, move, copy together). Fillets: bim_modify_detail. View feet for points, radii and distances, inches for sizes; on a sheet, paper inches. Points are {x, y}. Fields: line from, to; rect corner, opposite; circle center, radius; chain / polyline points, closed; arc center, start, end, clockwise; component symbol, at, width_in, height_in, rotation_deg, mirror; region points, hatch, masking; style keys line_style, weight, pattern, category, group. Every other shape's exact fields: bim_describe_commands({ tool: "bim_draw_detail", field: "items", variant: "<shape>" }). Dimensions: bim_add_dimension; notes: bim_add_note.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `owner`, `items`, `label`?

### bim_modify_detail

Change drafting items by id (from bim_list_view_annotations) with one operation, as one edit, on BIM drafting-view conventions. Detail lines joined end to end stay joined: moving, rotating, trimming or dragging an end stretches the joined line that wasn't picked (move disjoin: true leaves it). Operations: move / copy by dx, dy; rotate (about a centre, optionally a copy); scale; mirror about an axis (optionally a copy); array / polar_array (group: each copy its own detail group); align; offset lines, arcs and circles by a distance toward a side (pick a whole joined chain, e.g. a rectangle's four sides, and the corners still meet; copy: false moves them); trim_extend_corner (two items, a point on the part of each to keep); trim_extend_single (one item to a boundary, keep point); trim_extend_multiple (many items to one boundary, one keep point each); split (at a point; delete_to removes the piece between two points); split_gap; fillet_arc (two lines, radius; near1/near2 pick the parts to keep); chamfer; move_end (drag one end); pin / unpin (pinned items refuse to move, change shape or delete); delete; match_type (take source_id's line style and category). A rectangle drawn before joined lines existed becomes four joined lines on its first edit (ids <rect id>~s0..s3, in the same undo); naming it with two keep / near points picks the two sides at that corner. Items in a detail group bring the rest of their group (except the trims, splits, fillet, offset, move_end, match_type and delete, which act on exactly the items named). Dimensions that follow edited items update by themselves. Same units as bim_draw_detail (distance, radius and gap in view feet). Points are {x, y}. Fields: move / copy dx, dy (move disjoin); rotate center, angle_deg, copy; mirror axis_from, axis_to, copy; offset distance, toward, copy; trim_extend_corner keep1, keep2; trim_extend_single boundary_id, keep; split at, delete_to; fillet_arc radius, near1, near2; move_end end, to. Every other operation's exact fields: bim_describe_commands({ tool: "bim_modify_detail", field: "operation", variant: "<op>" }).

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `owner`, `item_ids`, `operation`

### bim_copy_detail_items

Copy drawing items (by id, or every item when item_ids is absent) from one view or sheet into another (detail view, plan, section or sheet), shifted by dx / dy in the target's units. Dimensions among them that follow other copied items follow the copies; detail groups stay together. Use it to start a new detail from an existing one.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `from`, `to`, `item_ids`?, `dx`?, `dy`?

### bim_set_detail_group

Put drawing items in a detail group (they then select, move, copy and modify together), or take them out (group: null).

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `owner`, `item_ids`, `group`

## Duct and pipe runs

Family `ducts-pipes`: Route, connect, resize, slope, insulate and fit duct and pipe runs.

Turn it on: `/packs/ducts-pipes/mcp`, `--packs ducts-pipes`, or `bim_enable_pack` in a session.

### bim_route_run

Route a duct or pipe run through plan points (feet), from / to a part's connector, an open run end, or the side of a trunk (a new tap, tee or wye by the system's rules); from / to may be on another level, heights staying from level_id's floor. Drops, elbows, transitions and the branch fitting are created with it, all or nothing, and the connectors are linked. Duct legs run level at any plan angle (the Route tool snaps; give any angle), plumb, or at a 45° slope, each elbow made to its turn (up to 135°) with that angle's loss; elbow types made only for 45° / 90° (mitred with vanes) refuse other turns. Pipe legs run E-W, N-S or 45° and turn 45° or 90°. Rises, fitting choices, insulation, sizing from airflow and the person's saved defaults: see the fields.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `level_id`, `kind`, `width_in`?, `height_in`?, `oval`?, `diameter_in`?, `nominal_in`?, `material`?, `spec`?, `elevation_ft`?, `points_ft`, `rise_style`?, `elbow_family`?, `takeoff_family`?, `from`?, `to`?, `system_id`?, `system_kind`?, `system_name`?, `cap_end`?, `slope_in_per_ft`?, `drain_flow`?, `insulation`?, `airflow_cfm`?, `duct_shape`?, `use_my_defaults`?

### bim_connect_runs

Connect existing duct or pipe, as one edit: two open ends that meet face to face (or an end to a part's connector, or two parts' connectors end to end); mode auto_route joins two open ends that don't meet with a square route (one rise or drop) worked out between them; tap_into_side continues an open end straight into another level run's side with a tap at that run's height (the Select tool's drag of an end onto a duct); tee_at_elbow turns a level elbow into a tee so a branch can continue from the corner (the + on an elbow). Run sizes and systems must match (two parts join anyway, mismatches reported); anything that can't be made is refused with the reason and nothing changes.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `a_id`, `a_end`, `b_id`?, `b_end`?, `mode`?

### bim_disconnect_run

Cut one connection; both sides are left open. Nothing is deleted.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `element_id`, `end`

### bim_route_flex

Flex from an open duct end into an air device's neck: round, sized to the neck, linked both ends. Refused if the end isn't the neck's size; warns past 6 ft.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `from_run_id`, `from_end`, `to_part_id`, `to_connector`?

### bim_resize_run

Change a run's size: rectangular, round or flat oval duct, or pipe (nominal size + material). The connected segments and elbows of the same size follow; transitions and branch takeoffs on the edge take the new size; a size a connector or fitting cannot take is refused with the reason.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `width_in`?, `height_in`?, `oval`?, `diameter_in`?, `nominal_in`?, `material`?, `spec`?, `element_id`?, `segment_id`?

### bim_slide_branch

Move a branch takeoff (a duct tap, or a routed tap, tee or wye on duct or pipe) to a new distance along its trunk. The trunk stays whole; connected pieces follow and parts stay put; if that is impossible you get the reason and nothing changes.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `distance_ft`, `element_id`?, `tap_id`?

### bim_set_terminal_airflow

Set a diffuser or grille's design airflow (CFM). Totals up the system recompute.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `cfm`, `element_id`?, `terminal_id`?

### bim_move_equipment

Move a unit by an offset in feet. Its connected ducts follow where they can.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `dx_ft`, `dy_ft`, `element_id`?, `equipment_id`?

### bim_resize_riser

Resize a riser through every level it crosses, as one change.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `width_in`?, `height_in`?, `diameter_in`?, `element_id`?, `riser_id`?

### bim_list_fitting_types

The fitting library: every family routing can place, what it fits, and its parameters. Duct: elbows, transitions, offsets, takeoffs, caps. Pipe: domestic water, drainage / waste / vent and fuel gas fittings with their joints, materials, take-out, and for drainage which direction changes each may make (rules to check against the adopted code). Use the id with bim_swap_fitting, bim_set_system_design or bim_place_pipe_accessory.

Input: `domain`?, `service`?

### bim_swap_fitting

Change a routed fitting to another library type (radius elbow r/W, mitred with turning vanes, 3/4/5-gore round, concentric / eccentric / rect-to-round transition, straight / 45° entry / conical / bellmouth / boot tap, lateral…). Same fitting, same connections. On the same type, params given change and the rest stay: an eccentric transition's flat side moves with params { flat: top | bottom | left | right } (Mirror = the opposite side) and keeps its wall angle. A type that can't be that fitting, or doesn't fit the duct beside it, is refused with the reason. Resizing a run to another shape swaps fittings not made in it (a smooth radius elbow on round duct becomes the system's round elbow) and says so.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `family`, `params`?, `element_id`?, `fitting_id`?

### bim_offset_run

Jog a routed duct or pipe run left, right, up or down at a point, with two 45° elbows, two 90° elbows or one ogee offset. With length_ft the run comes back in line and both ends stay; without it everything beyond moves with it (connected parts that can't follow refuse).

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `at_ft`, `side`, `distance_in`, `length_ft`?, `style`, `element_id`?, `segment_id`?

### bim_change_elevation

Raise or drop a stretch of a level run to a new height with 45° or 90° rises, back to the old height at to_ft, or to the end of the run (what is connected follows).

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `from_ft`, `to_ft`?, `elevation_ft`, `style`, `element_id`?, `segment_id`?

### bim_split_run

Cut a routed duct or pipe segment in two at a point (a plain joint). Both pieces keep its size, system and connections; branches stay on the piece they sit on. A cut on a takeoff, or one leaving a piece too short for its fittings, is refused with the reason.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `at_ft`, `element_id`?, `segment_id`?

### bim_resize_stretch

Give routed segments a new size or shape in one atomic edit (rectangular, round, flat oval, or pipe), optionally only between from_ft and to_ft on one segment. Elbows between resized pieces follow; where a neighbour keeps its size a transition is placed (the system's default, or concentric / eccentric flat top, bottom, left or right / rect-to-round), with the insulation of the duct it joins. Elbows, transitions and taps not made in the new shape take the system's choice for it (round duct gets the round elbow) and the result says which. Refused with the reason when a transition doesn't fit the straight duct beside it, or a branch would be as wide as its trunk.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `segment_ids`, `from_ft`?, `to_ft`?, `width_in`?, `height_in`?, `oval`?, `diameter_in`?, `nominal_in`?, `material`?, `spec`?, `transition`?

### bim_drag_run

Move one straight routed segment or in-line elbow by east_ft / north_ft / up_ft, as dragging it in the view does; what it meets follows (legs along the move stretch, legs square to it move, fixed parts refuse). A segment moves square to itself or along itself; a 45° or sloped piece between legs at an angle slides so those legs only stretch. With end, only that end moves (raise the top of a rise to make it taller). As dragging does, a leg pulled back past its elbow turns the other way (its 90° elbows flip), and a move that can't go all the way (a leg shorter than its elbows need, an elbow that can't flip) stops at the limit; the result says how far it moved and why. strict: true never flips and stops at the elbow limit instead. Refused only when it can't move that way at all.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `element_id`, `east_ft`?, `north_ft`?, `up_ft`?, `end`?, `strict`?, `stop_at_limit`?

### bim_set_system_design

Rename a system, or choose the fittings routing places on a system (per slot), and its design inputs: for duct, altitude, air temperature, duct material, the default insulation new runs get, and the sizing criteria bim_suggest_duct_size aims for; for pipe, pipe_design (water supply pressure, friction method, demand table, velocity limit; drain slopes, capacity table, direction-rule overrides; gas equation, specific gravity, allowable drop). No code tables are bundled: tables are the firm's own values.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `system_id`, `name`?, `altitude_ft`?, `temperature_f`?, `material`?, `fittings`?, `default_insulation`?, `sizing`?, `pipe_design`?

### bim_set_duct_insulation

Put an external wrap or internal liner (thickness in inches, optional material and R-value) on routed duct, or a wrap on pipe, or take it off: one piece, the run (stopping at transitions, branches and parts), or every duct or pipe of the system; from_schedule gives a pipe system the project's thickness by size. The size stays the sheet-metal size; a liner narrows the airway the pressure report uses (faced liner by default; surface spray_coated is rougher), a wrap grows the outside size. Fittings take the insulation of the duct they join. A liner that leaves less than 2" clear inside is refused with the reason.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `element_id`, `insulation`?, `scope`?, `from_schedule`?

### bim_set_slope

Pitch one level pipe segment (a drain) to a fall in inches per foot: one end stays, the other rises or drops, and what is connected beyond it follows (level runs move, vertical runs stretch, fixed fixtures refuse). Flatter than the system's minimum, or sloping a branch away from the run it drains into, is refused with the reason.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `in_per_ft`?, `flow`?, `keep`?, `element_id`?, `segment_id`?

### bim_place_pipe_accessory

Place a valve, union, coupling, cleanout, test tee, P-trap, gas cock, drip leg or gas regulator (params role, outlet_in_wc, zone_drop_in_wc: starts a pressure zone) inline on a pipe segment, at a distance from its start. Checked for service, material, joint, pipe direction and room.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `at_ft`, `family`, `params`?, `element_id`?, `segment_id`?

## Electrical circuits and diagrams

Family `electrical`: Panels, circuits, feeders, receptacle proposals, one-line and riser diagrams.

Turn it on: `/packs/electrical/mcp`, `--packs electrical`, or `bim_enable_pack` in a session.

### bim_electrical_report

Every panel, switchboard and transformer (or one, by id or name) with what it supplies and is fed from: connected load, NEC Article 220 demand by load class from the raw loads below it (220.56 kitchen equipment counted at each panel, so the MDP and the serving panel differ), the sizing load with continuous loads at 125% and the largest motor +25%, per-phase VA and amps, the true capacity with its limiting reason (bus, main, transformer kVA, feeding breaker, feeder conductors, what is left upstream), and findings (overloaded, unbalanced phases, a member whose voltage no longer matches, a bus bigger than its breaker, a load with nothing to count). One panel also lists its circuits and their members. The NEC edition is nec_edition, else the project's Code Study, else the state; with none of those the totals are connected loads only and say so. Read-only; no approval.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `panel`?, `include_circuits`?, `nec_edition`?, `state`?, `occupancy`?

### bim_read_panel

One panel as the Building Model's panel view draws it: every used slot with its circuit, breaker, poles and members, the free slots, and what feeds it. No panel: the devices on no circuit yet. Totals and capacity are in bim_electrical_report. Read-only.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `panel`?

### bim_electrical_catalog

The project's connection types (designator → load, voltage, poles, class), feeder types (mark → breaker, conductor sets, ground, conduit) and room templates. size_feeder_for: propose a feeder type for that panel from its NEC calculated load (breaker, conductors with voltage drop, parallel sets, EGC, conduit, with clauses) to save with bim_save_electrical_type. check: the Electrical tab's check list (overloads, unbalance, voltage mismatch, breakers vs nameplate, loads on no circuit). Read-only.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `kind`?, `size_feeder_for`?, `length_ft`?, `material`?, `conduit`?, `check`?, `nec_edition`?

### bim_propose_links_from_text

Read the circuit numbers people typed on devices ("L1-3", "HP1-43,45") and the "Fed from" typed on panels ("MDP"), and return, for each circuit or feeder, what would be made, whether the model allows it (with the reason when not), and the exact arguments for bim_create_circuit or bim_add_to_circuit. Devices are grouped only when their own text names the same panel and circuit numbers. Nothing is changed: show the person the proposals and make only the ones they confirm, one approval each. Read-only; no approval.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`

### bim_preview_circuit_edit

Dry run of a circuit, rebalance, catalog or room-template edit tool at the revision you read: what it changes (a rebalance's moves, a template's circuits per unit), or the plain reason it would be refused. Saves nothing; no approval.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `tool`, `args`

### bim_create_circuit

Serve the listed devices or equipment from a panel's breaker (a branch circuit), or another panel or transformer from a breaker in this one (a feeder; a transformer's secondary feeds its panel with no breaker). Members are exactly what the person asked for. Positions are the panel's circuit numbers (one per pole: 1,3,5 for three poles); leave them out to take the lowest free ones that fit. The breaker defaults to one piece of equipment's MOCP, else 20 A; a feeder's to the fed panel's main, else its bus. Refused in plain words when voltage, poles, phases or free positions don't allow it (e.g. a 480 V unit on a 120/208 V panel): say the reason as written. A retried identical call is refused as already made. Pauses for the person's approval.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `source_id`, `members`, `positions`?, `description`?, `breaker_a`?, `frame_a`?, `load_class`?, `conductors`?, `length_ft`?, `feeder_type`?, `circuit_id`?, `one_circuit_each`?

### bim_edit_circuit

Move a circuit or feeder to other positions or another panel (its members are checked again), or change its breaker, frame, load class, conductors, length, feeder type or description. null clears a value. Members don't change here (bim_add_to_circuit, bim_remove_from_circuit). An existing circuit on a renovation (built in the Existing phase: bim_set_element_phases on its id) keeps its panel and slots. Refused in plain words when the move isn't allowed. Pauses for the person's approval.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `circuit_id`, `source_id`?, `positions`?, `description`?, `breaker_a`?, `frame_a`?, `load_class`?, `conductors`?, `length_ft`?, `feeder_type`?

### bim_add_to_circuit

Put the listed devices or equipment on an existing circuit (exactly those). Each is checked against the panel's voltage and the circuit's poles; refused in plain words otherwise, and a device already on a circuit is refused. Pauses for the person's approval.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `circuit_id`, `members`

### bim_remove_from_circuit

Take the listed devices or equipment off a circuit. The circuit stays, even empty (a spare); delete it with bim_delete_elements. Pauses for the person's approval.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `circuit_id`, `element_ids`

### bim_feed_panel

Feed a panel or transformer from a breaker in another board or panel, or from a transformer's secondary; a feeder it already has moves instead of a second one being made. Refused in plain words on a mismatch (a 120/208 V panel off a 480 V board needs a transformer between; never add one yourself, ask). Pauses for the person's approval.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `panel_id`, `source_id`, `positions`?, `breaker_a`?, `feeder_type`?

### bim_rebalance_panel

Move or swap circuits on one panel so its phases carry more even load (deterministic: the same model gives the same moves; three-pole breakers and keep_circuits stay; what is on each circuit never changes). Preview the moves with bim_preview_circuit_edit first and show them. Pauses for approval.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `panel`, `keep_circuits`?, `max_moves`?

### bim_save_electrical_type

Add or change one catalog record; replaces renames it and what names it follows (devices' connection_type, feeders' feeder type). delete removes one nothing uses. Devices take a connection type through bim_set_parameters values.connection_type. Pauses for approval.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `entry`?, `replaces`?, `delete`?

### bim_apply_circuit_template

Circuit the devices in each unit's rooms by the firm's room template (bedroom → 1…). The person names each unit's rooms and panel; never choose a panel or rooms yourself. Devices already on a circuit are left alone; a refused circuit is reported, the rest are made. Preview with bim_preview_circuit_edit. Pauses for approval.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `template`, `units`

### bim_preview_one_line

Preview a diagram without saving: what it draws, warnings (bus vs feeding breaker), size, and would_save with a preview_token for bim_layout_one_line. from_model: true (the normal case) makes a LIVE diagram drawn from the model at every revision: kind one_line, electrical_riser, plumbing_riser (branches, sizes, running DFU/WFU/MBH; pipes listed) or plumbing_isometric, with layout hints; with view, an existing drafting view becomes live or gets new hints. diagram (static) is only for a distribution described by hand with no model: roots are utility/generator sources; children CT cabinet, meter, switchboard / panelboard / MCC with a main, transformer, ATS with its emergency generator, disconnects, VFD, UPS, motors; each with name, ratings and its feeder (device, label, sets, conductors, conduit, length). Free; no approval.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `view`?, `replace_existing`?, `new_view_name`?, `diagram`?, `from_model`?, `kind`?, `hints`?, `place_on`?

### bim_layout_one_line

Save what bim_preview_one_line previewed, as one change: a live diagram view (or its new hints), or the static drawing, and (place_on) its viewport on a sheet. Same arguments plus the preview's base_revision and preview_token; anything different is refused. A live diagram redraws itself when the model changes; change its layout by calling again with view and hints. Look at it after with bim_render_view_image.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `view`?, `replace_existing`?, `new_view_name`?, `diagram`?, `from_model`?, `kind`?, `hints`?, `place_on`?, `base_revision`, `preview_token`

### bim_propose_receptacles

Where receptacles of the chosen type would go in the picked rooms: 210.52 wall space, countertops, islands, bathrooms, laundry, hallways (needs the NEC edition), or a density preset (firm spacing, no code edition; code says so). Wall devices sit with their back on the wall face. Each device has a key, reason and clause; coverage says if every point is in reach. Read-only; accept with bim_accept_receptacles.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `rooms`, `mode`?, `preset`?, `wall_type`, `countertop_type`?, `bathroom_type`?, `room_rules`?, `nec_edition`?, `apply_to_similar`?

### bim_accept_receptacles

Re-runs the proposal at the revision you read and places the kept devices as one edit, uncircuited. Send the proposal's arguments. Pauses for approval.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `rooms`, `mode`?, `preset`?, `wall_type`, `countertop_type`?, `bathroom_type`?, `room_rules`?, `nec_edition`?, `apply_to_similar`?, `keep`?

### bim_place_service_layout

From a service size (yours or bim_service_from_equipment_list's): meter, optional main disconnect, MDP and the listed panels and transformers, each fed from what's named, as one edit. Ask for every rating; nothing is sized. Pauses for approval.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `level`, `origin_ft`?, `room`?, `service_a`, `system`, `meter`?, `main_disconnect`?, `plan_only`?, `distribution`?, `equipment`?

## Plumbing loads and design

Family `plumbing`: Fixture load points, connection types, pipe types and each pipe system's sizing.

Turn it on: `/packs/plumbing/mcp`, `--packs plumbing`, or `bim_enable_pack` in a session.

### bim_place_load_points

Put loads on open pipe ends or taps without fixtures (one batch, up to 500). Each names a connection type (WSFU/DFU/MBH/CFM come from it) or gives values; one point per end, per system (a sink: cold, hot and waste points sharing a mark). A type with no connection of the pipe's system is refused; points returns each point's pipe, system and loads, with warnings. Then read totals with bim_pipe_report. Pauses for approval.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `points`

### bim_edit_load_point

Any trade's loads. edit: type, values or source (served_by; part_id edits every point of an attached fixture). attach: the fixture the person named takes the point's connection type; totals unchanged. detach keeps the point. split: break a lump onto new points, totals preserved. delete. create: loads on a space/zone (an estimate), a part, a point or nowhere yet. move: same id to a new anchor (estimate → point → device). policy: how estimates count once devices exist. Pauses for approval.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `action`, `load_point_id`?, `part_id`?, `connection_type`?, `values`?, `reset`?, `mark`?, `into`?, `load_point_ids`?, `served_by`?, `clear_served_by`?, `loads`?, `to`?, `policy`?

### bim_save_connection_type

Add or change a connection type: trade plumbing/gas/mechanical/electrical, quantities (wsfu_cold, wsfu_hot, wsfu_total = the code's combined value, dfu, gph_demand, mbh, min_inlet_pressure in psi, cfm, sizes, custom; text with a unit like '7 in. w.c.' is converted). replaces renames it; delete removes one nothing uses. Pauses for approval.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `entry`?, `replaces`?, `delete`?

### bim_plumbing_catalog

Pipe types (material, spec, sizes, joint, systems, the fittings each slot takes: the material's unless picked), every pipe system's colour, line pattern, weight and own sizing, the project's auto-sizing, building type, demand curve and pipe insulation schedule, and the stacks (named or not: tag, size and DFU per floor, offsets). Read-only.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`

### bim_plumbing_design

One change. system_look: colour/pattern/weight (null: standard). system_sizing / project: sizing_mode, demand_curve (project also building_type, insulation_schedule). save_pipe_type / delete_pipe_type. Turn auto-sizing on only when the person asks: on, edits resize that system's pipes as they land. Pauses for approval.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `action`, `system`?, `colour`?, `pattern`?, `weight`?, `sizing_mode`?, `demand_curve`?, `building_type`?, `insulation_schedule`?, `insulation_source`?, `pipe_type`?, `replaces`?, `name`?

## Views and sheets

Family `views-sheets`: Views, crops, 3D views, sheets, viewports, sheet notes and layout.

Turn it on: `/packs/views-sheets/mcp`, `--packs views-sheets`, or `bim_enable_pack` in a session.

### bim_create_view

Create a floor plan or ceiling plan for a level, a section from a cut line (plan feet) with a look direction and depth, a 3D view, or a detail view (drawing-only: lines, text, dimensions). Returns the new view id. Refused with a plain reason if the name is taken or a plan has no level.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `name`, `view_type`, `level`?, `scale`?, `cut_height_ft`?, `section_start_ft`?, `section_end_ft`?, `section_looks`?, `section_depth_ft`?

### bim_set_view_properties

Set a view's scale, what a plan shows (top_ft, cut_height_ft, bottom_ft, view_depth_ft: our model and the linked models both follow them), line weights by category (line_weights; linked models take cut_line_weight / beyond_line_weight), linked-model simplification (linked_hidden_lines removes a chair under a table; linked_min_object_in leaves out small things), plan orientation (plan north, true north or the working angle up), discipline (others print halftone; null for all in ink), hidden categories, how each linked model draws (normal, halftone, transparent, underlay or hidden, a 3D see-through %, per-IFC-category exceptions; a person's working 3D view '{3D - name}' takes these too), detail level, or its crop box. The crop box is in feet in the view's own frame: plan x/y for plans and 3D views, along-the-cut distance by elevation for sections, drawing feet for detail views. crop_view off shows everything; show_crop_box only changes what editors see (the boundary never prints); annotation_crop lets notes and tags reach past the crop; far_clip_ft sets how far a section sees; fit_crop sizes the crop to the view's content (send it on its own). A placed view's viewport resizes with its crop. Give the view by id or exact name.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `view`, `scale`?, `cut_height_ft`?, `discipline`?, `hidden_categories`?, `hidden_drafting_categories`?, `linked_models`?, `detail_level`?, `crop_min_ft`?, `crop_max_ft`?, `fit_crop`?, `keep_viewport_center`?, `crop_view`?, `show_crop_box`?, `annotation_crop`?, `annotation_crop_offset_in`?, `far_clip_ft`?, `orientation`?, `projection`?, `top_ft`?, `bottom_ft`?, `view_depth_ft`?, `line_weights`?, `linked_hidden_lines`?, `linked_min_object_in`?, `category_overrides`?

### bim_rename_view

Rename a view. Refused if another view has that name. Its sheet titles follow.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `view`, `name`

### bim_duplicate_view

Copy a view with its properties and crop (and a detail view's drawing) under a new name (default "<name> Copy"). The copy isn't on a sheet. Use it to show the same plan twice, e.g. an enlarged plan.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `view`, `name`?

### bim_delete_view

Delete a view. A view placed on a sheet is refused unless if_placed is remove_from_sheet (its viewport goes too). Undo brings it back.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `view`, `if_placed`?

### bim_create_sheet

Create a sheet with a number, name, title block (ARCH D 36x24 by default, or ANSI B 17x11) and title block fields (client, address, drawn_by, checked_by, date, status). Refused if the number is taken.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `number`, `name`, `title_block`?, `fields`?

### bim_set_sheet_properties

Change a sheet's number, name, title block size, title block fields (client, address, drawn_by, checked_by, date, status, or any other key; an empty string clears one), and its revision table: add_revision appends one row; revisions replaces the whole table (oldest first). Refused if the number is taken, a revision number repeats, or a smaller title block can't hold its viewports.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `sheet`, `number`?, `name`?, `title_block`?, `fields`?, `add_revision`?, `revisions`?

### bim_delete_sheet

Delete a sheet with its viewports, notes and linework. Its views are kept (no longer placed). Undo brings it back.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `sheet`

### bim_place_viewport

Place a view on a sheet as a viewport, centred at a paper position in inches from the sheet's top-left, at the view's scale or the one given. A view goes on one sheet only; the refusal names the sheet it is already on.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `sheet`, `view`, `center_in`, `scale`?

### bim_edit_viewport

Change a placed view on its sheet. action move: centre_in on paper (inches from the sheet's top-left). resize: the frame's size_in (the view's crop box follows at the viewport's scale; optional centre_in). scale: a new drawing scale (the frame grows or shrinks; the crop box stays). A live diagram or schedule is its own size: move only. A frame past the drawing area saves with a warning. north_arrow: show or hide. remove: take it off the sheet (the view is kept). Name the viewport by its view's name or id (optionally the sheet), or the viewport id. To place many at once, use bim_auto_layout_sheet.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `viewport`, `sheet`?, `action`, `center_in`?, `size_in`?, `scale`?, `show`?

### bim_preview_sheet_layout

Work out where every viewport on a sheet should go, without saving: frames packed in rows (or an aligned grid) inside the border and left of the title block, with room under each for its title; optionally shrinking a view's scale to fit. Same model, same answer every time. Returns the moves, any view that can't fit (and why), and a preview_token for bim_auto_layout_sheet.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `sheet`, `mode`?, `columns`?, `gap_in`?, `fit_scales`?, `smallest_scale`?, `order`?

### bim_auto_layout_sheet

Apply the layout bim_preview_sheet_layout returned, as one edit: same arguments, its base_revision and preview_token. Refused if the model changed since the preview (the layout would differ): preview again.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `sheet`, `mode`?, `columns`?, `gap_in`?, `fit_scales`?, `smallest_scale`?, `order`?, `base_revision`, `preview_token`

### bim_set_issue_status

Read only, issues nothing: whether every sheet draws as in the last set print (and which differ or weren't printed), the revision to pass bim_issue_set as expected_revision, the next revision number, the last print, earlier issues (newest first, with 5-minute PDF links), and each live block: Live, Matches or Changed since its last issue.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `sheets`?

### bim_add_sheet_note

Write a note on a sheet: a box at a paper position (inches from the top-left) that wraps its text at width_in. Plain text, or rich paragraphs with bold, italic, underline, bullets, numbered lists (with levels), alignment and per-run text height. It prints exactly as people see it. Use bim_preview_views_sheets_edit with create_text_note to check it first. Characters outside letters, numbers and drafting symbols are refused with the reason.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `sheet`, `text`?, `paragraphs`?, `at_in`, `width_in`?, `height_in`?, `rotation_deg`?, `leader_to_in`?, `text_height_in`?

### bim_edit_text_note

Replace a note's whole text (on a sheet or in a detail view) with plain text or rich paragraphs, keeping its box and position. Pass expected_content from bim_list_views_and_sheets: if anyone changed the note's words since you read it, nothing is saved and the result says so. Read again and re-plan.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `note`, `expected_content`, `text`?, `paragraphs`?

### bim_create_3d_view

Create a saved 3D view, pre-cropped: of_elements (or region_ft) fits its 3D crop box to them, grown out to the floor and next level and the grid lines around them (a storey and bay, never a tight box); box_ft sets the box exactly; neither crops to the whole model. look_from picks the camera (default south_west isometric). place_on puts it on a sheet in the same approval, e.g. an isometric of a mechanical room. On sheets it prints as vector hidden-line from its camera, cropped to the whole box. Returns the new view id.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `name`, `of_elements`?, `region_ft`?, `box_ft`?, `look_from`?, `projection`?, `place_on`?

### bim_set_3d_view_camera

Point a saved 3D view's camera: look_from a named direction at its crop box, or eye_ft and target_ft exactly (feet). Optionally switch projection. The view opens from here and prints from here; a placed viewport's frame resizes to the box as seen from the new camera.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `view`, `look_from`?, `eye_ft`?, `target_ft`?, `projection`?

### bim_set_3d_crop_box

Size, fit, or switch a saved 3D view's 3D crop box: box_ft sets it exactly; fit 'selection' with element_ids (or region_ft) grows it to the storey and grid bay around them; fit 'model' puts it back around the whole model (square to the working angle). align 'working_angle' turns the box about its middle to the view's working angle, or align with from_ft/to_ft turns it square to a building edge; its size is kept (there is no rotate handle on the box; this is how it turns). crop_on false shows everything (the box is kept); show_box only changes what people editing see (it never prints). It crops live and on sheets, heights included; a placed viewport's frame follows.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `view`, `box_ft`?, `fit`?, `element_ids`?, `region_ft`?, `crop_on`?, `show_box`?, `align`?

## Coordination and linked models

Family `coordination`: Linked models, levels from them, coordinates, accepted findings and rooms.

Turn it on: `/packs/coordination/mcp`, `--packs coordination`, or `bim_enable_pack` in a session.

### bim_browse_autodesk_docs

List a folder of the project's Autodesk Docs project (top folders when folder_id is left out), or search below it by name. Each file says whether it can be linked and why not, and which linked model it already is. Needs model edit access and the person's Autodesk sign-in (Settings), like Link a model › From Autodesk Docs. Then bim_link_from_autodesk_docs.

Input: `project_id`, `folder_id`?, `query`?

### bim_link_from_autodesk_docs

Bring up to 25 Revit or IFC files from the project's Autodesk Docs into the Building Model as linked models, each with the name people see and its discipline. A file already linked adds a new version to that linked model. Autodesk exports and converts them in the background; bim_list_linked_models shows progress. Needs model edit access and the person's Autodesk sign-in.

Input: `project_id`, `items`

### bim_update_linked_model

The Linked models panel's actions on one linked model: check Docs for a newer version or export it again, line it up with the project model, export our own Revit model again, try a failed conversion again, show another converted version, or save a position adjustment (feet and degrees from where it was placed; give only what changes). What changes is seen by everyone on the project. Read bim_list_linked_models first.

Input: `project_id`, `action`, `reference_id`?, `version_id`?, `east_ft`?, `north_ft`?, `up_ft`?, `rotation_deg`?

### bim_unlink_linked_model

Take a linked model out of the Building Model for everyone on the project. Its files and versions are kept, and a conversion still running won't bring it back; linking it again from Docs or an upload adds it anew. Views that showed it stop drawing it.

Input: `project_id`, `reference_id`

### bim_sync_linked_levels

Make the model's levels match a linked model's storeys in one undoable change: a level for each storey not yet made, and the levels made from storeys updated where the architect moved or renamed them. A level a person already made for the same floor (same name or elevation) is tied to the storey and keeps its name. Nothing is deleted; running it again when nothing changed is refused with that reason. Defaults to the architectural model.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `linked_model_id`?

### bim_update_level

Move a level to a new floor elevation (feet) and/or rename it. Everything on the level moves with it (parts and runs keep their height above it); plans, schedules and elements that name the level follow a rename. Refused if another level has the name.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `level_id`, `name`?, `elevation_ft`?

### bim_create_level

Add a level (storey) with a name and floor elevation in feet. Parts are placed on levels.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `name`, `elevation_ft`

### bim_read_coordinates

Where the model sits: the project base point and survey point (model feet and site N/S, E/W, elevation in feet), the internal origin, true north (degrees clockwise from plan north), the working angle (the model's and any view's own) and the placement an IFC export carries. Read before changing coordinates.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`

### bim_preview_coordinates_edit

Dry run of bim_set_project_origin, bim_set_survey_point, bim_set_true_north or bim_set_working_angle at the latest revision: what would change, or the reason it would be refused. Saves nothing and needs no approval.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `tool`, `args`

### bim_set_project_origin

Either move only the base point on the model (move_point: everything keeps its site coordinates) or relocate the project on the site (relocate_project: geometry stays put, every element's site coordinates change by the same move, the survey point stays on the site). Feet.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `mode`, `position`?, `shared`?

### bim_set_survey_point

The same two moves as the Coordinates dialog's survey point: move only its marker on the model (move_point: nobody's site coordinates change), or give it the site coordinates it should read (relocate_project: the site moves under the building, every element's site coordinates change, geometry and linked models stay put). Feet. Read bim_read_coordinates first.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `mode`, `position`?, `shared`?

### bim_set_true_north

Set the angle from plan north to true north (degrees clockwise), or give two plan points along true north. Turns the building on the site about the project base point; geometry and plans drawn plan-north do not move.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `angle_deg`?, `from_ft`?, `to_ft`?

### bim_set_working_angle

Turn the directions people draw in to match a skewed building: give angle_deg, or two plan points along a building edge (from_ft, to_ft) and the axes turn square to it. Route snaps (square and 45°), the placement grid, drafting ortho/polar and new 3D crop boxes follow it; plans set to orientation 'working_angle' draw turned to it. With view, it applies to that view only (use_model_angle drops the view's own). Never moves geometry, linked models, site coordinates or true north.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `angle_deg`?, `from_ft`?, `to_ft`?, `view`?, `use_model_angle`?

### bim_lint_accept_finding

Accept a finding with the person's reason (hidden for everyone until its elements change). Only when the person says so. finding_id must be an id from bim_lint_check now; any other id is refused.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `finding_id`, `reason`, `check_only`?

### bim_lint_retract_acceptance

Undo an acceptance (one made by mistake, or no longer true) with the person's reason: the finding shows again; who accepted, who retracted and why are kept. Only when the person says so.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `finding_id`, `reason`, `check_only`?

### bim_trace_rooms

Adds rooms (outline in feet) with a wall on each edge, doors, windows and counters or fixtures, as one edit, so proposers can measure them. Trace only what the plan shows. Pauses for approval.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `level`, `rooms`, `openings`?, `casework`?, `wall_thickness_in`?

## Groups, phases and typed elements

Family `groups-phases`: Groups, locks, phases, phase filters and typed element values.

Turn it on: `/packs/groups-phases/mcp`, `--packs groups-phases`, or `bim_enable_pack` in a session.

### bim_list_groups_and_phases

The model's groups (name, colour, locked, default visibility), phases in time order, phase filters (how new / existing / demolished / temporary elements draw), the active group and phase new work goes in, and each view's phase, filter and group visibility. include_counts adds elements per group (reads the whole model; skip on very large models unless needed). Every element is in one group; elements with no group are in General, with no phase are built in New construction.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `include_counts`?

### bim_preview_organization_edit

Run one groups/phases command against the latest revision without saving: what would change, or the plain reason it would be refused (a locked group, a phase in use, demolished before built). Commands: create_group, update_group, lock_group, delete_group (moveTo), set_active_group, assign_elements_to_group, create_phase, update_phase (after), delete_phase, set_active_phase, set_element_phases, demolish_elements, undemolish_elements, create_phase_filter, update_phase_filter, delete_phase_filter, set_group_typical (repeat a unit: array { count, columns, spacingMm } or copies; its loads count once per copy where it is served from outside), clear_group_typical. Ids, not names.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `command`

### bim_create_group

Add a group (e.g. 'Phase 2 tenant fit-out'). New work goes in it only once it is made active. Refused if the name is taken.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `name`, `color`?, `description`?, `default_visibility`?

### bim_update_group

Rename a group, change its colour, description or default visibility, or lock / unlock it. Locked: nobody (people or agents) can create, change, move, demolish or delete its elements until it is unlocked. typical repeats the group (unit 001 x24: copies draw on plans and count in every trade's totals: drain, service, meter, project); typical null stops. Send locked or typical on its own call.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `group`, `name`?, `color`?, `description`?, `default_visibility`?, `locked`?, `typical`?

### bim_delete_group

Delete a group. If elements are in it, give move_to (the group they go to); without it a group with elements is refused. General can't be deleted. Undo brings the group back.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `group`, `move_to`?

### bim_assign_to_group

Move elements (a run, a branch, a box selection's ids) into a group. Refused, with nothing changed, if any of them, or the target, is in a locked group.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `element_ids`, `group`

### bim_set_active_group_and_phase

Set the model's active group (new ducts, pipes and parts go in it) or active phase (new elements are built in it; demolish uses it), typical_cap, switch an add-on on or off for this model (addon), or branch: start one (Main is untouched) or propose this thread's branch to Main; people approve merges. Give one of them per call. A locked group can't be made active.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `group`?, `phase`?, `typical_cap`?, `addon`?, `branch`?

### bim_create_phase

Add a phase in time order: after a named phase, first (after: null), or last (after absent).

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `name`, `after`?

### bim_update_phase

Rename a phase, or move it in time (after: a phase, or null for first). Moving is refused if something would be demolished before it is built.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `phase`, `name`?, `after`?

### bim_set_element_phases

Set the phase elements are built in and/or demolished in (demolished_in: null = not demolished), or action 'demolish' (in the given phase, default the active phase) / 'restore' (not demolished). Refused if something would be demolished before it is built, or is in a locked group.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `element_ids`, `action`?, `built_in`?, `demolished_in`?, `phase`?

### bim_set_view_organization

Set which phase a view shows the model as of, its phase filter, and per group show / halftone / hide in that view (only the groups given change). This reaches the live canvas, the printed drawing, sheets and PDF.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `view`, `phase`?, `phase_filter`?, `groups`?

### bim_set_phase_filter

Create a phase filter (give name and all four statuses) or change one (give filter and any of name / statuses). Each status draws as show, halftone, dashed or hide. new = built in the view's phase; existing = built earlier and still there; demolished = removed in the view's phase; temporary = built and removed in it.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `filter`?, `name`?, `new`?, `existing`?, `demolished`?, `temporary`?

### bim_delete_phase

Delete a phase nothing uses. Refused, with the reason, if any element is built or demolished in it, a view shows it, it is the default phase, or it is the last one. Undo brings it back.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `phase`

### bim_delete_phase_filter

Delete a phase filter no view uses. Refused, with the views that use it, otherwise; the last filter can't be deleted. Undo brings it back.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `filter`

### bim_set_element

One change per call on walls, slabs, openings, rooms, grids, columns, beams and components: class, type_id, values (by parameter key; a part takes its add-on keys here), place (geometry in plan feet), lock (existing or issued, with a reason; false unlocks), new_type (a shared type to set with type_id) or code. Preview with bim_preview_part_edit.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `element_ids`?, `class`?, `type_id`?, `values`?, `place`?, `lock`?, `new_type`?, `code`?, `architecture`?

## Part definitions

Family `parts`: Draft, check and save parts, the firm's part library, clearances and hosts.

Turn it on: `/packs/parts/mcp`, `--packs parts`, or `bim_enable_pack` in a session.

### bim_draft_part_from_cut_sheet

Draft a part (rooftop unit, air terminal, water heater) from a cut sheet PDF on the project. Returns the sheet text by page, each fact (dimensions, openings, connections, electrical, capacity, model) cited to page and line, assumptions, and a checked part definition. Saves nothing. Fix what's wrong (bim_check_part_definition), then save with bim_save_part_definition or bim_save_firm_part (both pause for approval).

Input: `project_id`, `file_id`?, `file_url`?, `kind`?, `part_name`?

### bim_read_picture_rows

Equipment schedule (picture or PDF on the project) to planned rows. First call saves nothing: rows (page, values, check_this) and next steps. Commit: rows, type_id, file_name, base_revision, preview_token, user_confirmed (pauses for approval).

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `file_id`, `hint`?, `type_id`?, `file_name`?, `rows`?, `preview_token`?, `user_confirmed`?

### bim_part_definition_example

A complete, valid part definition to start from (rooftop_unit: box on a hollow curb with a cut-in panel, two duct and one power connector, three sizes; floor_drain: revolved body and outlet with a strainer symbol), plus a short guide to every field. Use it as the template for bim_check_part_definition and bim_save_part_definition.

Input: `example`

### bim_check_part_definition

Dry run of a part definition: every problem in plain words (formulas, sketches that don't close or can't be solved, features without depth, connectors, each size in the types table), then for each size its type id, overall size, connector positions and sizes (warnings for one below the base, inside the body or facing into it), and plan / front / side previews as SVG. Saves nothing. Fix and re-check until status is ok, then save with bim_save_part_definition.

Input: `part_name`, `definition`, `preview_type`?, `previews`?

### bim_read_part_definition

Open a part the way Edit part does: give a part type id (bim_list_part_types) or a placed part's id, get back part_name and definition in exactly the form bim_check_part_definition and bim_save_part_definition take (reference planes, sketches, features, connectors, parameters and the types table), its sizes and how many are placed. Change it, check, save with the same part_name.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `id`

### bim_save_part_definition

Save a modeled part (made with the part editor's model: reference planes, sketches, extrudes and revolves, connectors, a types table) to the project library. Each row of its types table becomes a placeable type with id <model id>.<size>; placed parts of an existing type update at once. Refused, with the reason, if the definition doesn't check out or if a run is connected to a connector it would remove or move.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `level`?, `zone`?, `base_revision`?, `part_name`, `definition`

### bim_list_firm_parts

Parts in the firm library, which every project can place: name, category, every size's type id, revision and where each came from (e.g. its cut sheet). Place one with bim_place_part, type_id = a size's type id and from_firm_library = true.

Input: `search`?, `category`?

### bim_save_firm_part

Save a modeled part definition (from the part editor, bim_read_part_definition or bim_draft_part_from_cut_sheet) to the firm library, where every project can place it. A part with the same model id is replaced (its revision goes up; projects that already placed it keep their copy until they save it again). Refused, with the reason, if the definition doesn't check out. Pauses for approval.

Input: `part_name`, `definition`

### bim_set_clearances

Space a part needs kept clear: service access, combustibles, economizer access, NEC 110.26 working space. Zones draw dashed, are never solid, move with the part; lint's clearance-intrusion reports anything inside one. scope type: zones replace the type's (every placed part follows). scope instance: overrides by zone id for this part (null clears; a full zone adds one). working_space computes depth/width/height from Table 110.26(A)(1) for the voltage and condition you choose.

Input: `project_id`, `model_id`, `base_revision`?, `element_id`, `scope`, `zones`?, `overrides`?, `working_space`?, `dedicated_space`?

### bim_set_part_host
